label: Incident File
line: Start on the moment of failure or its price. Rewind to an ordinary person making a reasonable wrong call, raise an alarm at every beat with one sentence of mechanism each, then the cause and the cost.
best_for: an outage, a loss or a bug with a timeline
any real incident with a public account that gives times and numbers
also_for: the fall of a product or a company, told through one day
avoid_for: an incident with no decision by a person
a cause that needs a tutorial before the story can go on

beats.name: Cold open
beats.job: The fatal action said casually, or the price as a number.

beats.name: Rewind
beats.job: A time stamp, the organisation in one line, and an unnamed person (by role) about to make the call.

beats.name: Alarm 1 and the wrong call
beats.job: The first symptom and a reasonable wrong assumption.

beats.name: Alarm 2
beats.job: It gets worse. One sentence explains the one mechanism the story needs here.

beats.name: The act
beats.job: The spoken re-opening: the fix they reached for, or the fatal action again, now understood.

beats.name: Before and after
beats.job: The number pair: what it was, what it became.

hooks.shape: Imagine [losing a large number] by [one tiny action]. [Organisation] nearly did.
'[A casual line announcing the fatal action]. It should be safe.'
At [time] on [date], [a person, by role] [ran one routine thing], and within [short time] [the symptoms].

holds: The viewer knows the ending and the people in the story do not. A number in every beat. Facts come in the order an investigation finds them (effect, then cause, then the contradiction), never in calendar order. A spoken re-opening at about three fifths.
ending: The before-and-after pair, then one dry kicker. No list of lessons.
first_frame: The fatal action in progress (the command being typed, the switch being thrown) or the cost as a number racing up and locking.
pitfalls: Inventing an incident or its numbers: every figure needs a source
Telling it from the victims' side
template: [The price, or the fatal line]. [Organisation] was [doing X] with [tool], [one-clause gloss]. At [time], [first symptom]. [The person, by role] assumed [a reasonable wrong cause]. Then [second symptom, with a number]. [The mechanism, in one sentence]. The fix? [One sentence], because [cause]. After that, [metric] went from [before] to [after]. [Kicker].
